title: 0•X — BCH Prototype
author: aeturnis-dev
selftext:
You wake on a small ship. Its power, cooling, air, and propulsion are simulated systems that actually work and actually fail, and the computer running it is a genuine emulated 16-bit processor with its own instruction set,

  running a Forth operating system on a memory-mapped device bus. You walk up to the CRT, sit down, and program it live.

  The core loop is diagnosis: authored failure scenarios you figure out from the inside and fix two different ways, one at the terminal, one by hand (breakers, switches, hatches).

  
It was originally and heavily inspired by **0x10c(**Notch/Mojang) for the premise, but design and philosphy has diverged greatly.

  
[Itch.io Download](https://aeturnis-development-labs.itch.io/0x)

  
>!What this project builds on!<

>!\- The DCPU‑16 is a 16‑bit CPU design Notch published openly in 2012; an ecosystem of open‑source!<

>!  emulators and tools grew around its public specification. The emulator in crates/dcpu/ is our!<

>!  own implementation of that instruction set.!<

>!\- The 2012 prototype (SpaceGame) was recovered locally and used as a reference. The recovered!<

>!  build itself — decompiled source, dcpu.jar, and its original assets — is Mojang's copyright!<

>!  and is NOT included in this repository (it is git‑ignored at 0x10c(proto)/).!<



>!Independently authored (no prototype‑derived code or assets on the shipping path)!<



>!As of the AeturnisOS work, the game's computing stack is our own original work:!<



>!\- crates/asm — our DCPU‑16 assembler (replaces the prototype's dcpu.jar build path).!<

>!\- crates/aos — AeturnisOS: our boot ROM, POST, machine monitor, and indirect‑threaded Forth,!<

>!  assembled by crates/asm. The app boots this image; it no longer boots the old boot.bin.!<

>!\- crates/app/assets/font.rom — our original 8×12 font for the Aeturnis Text Display Controller!<

>!  (ATDC/1), generated by pipeline/font/gen\_font.py. Every glyph is drawn by us.!<
